items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to release refund
items.quote: Damit wir sie auszahlen können, überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for the payment: 'bis zum 27.11.2026' (by 27 November 2026). No deemed-delivery or statutory period calculation applies, since this is a fixed date stated by a non-authority sender. Taking the date as written: due_date = 2026-11-27. However, the entire demand shows the hallmarks of an advance-fee scam (see warnings): there is no real legal obligation to pay this 'fee', so the date is recorded only as what the letter itself demands, not as a genuine deadline.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: it promises a sizeable refund (612,00 €) but demands an upfront 'processing fee' (49,90 €) before anything is paid out — a classic fraud pattern, never a real German authority practice.

The payment IBAN (CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600) is a Cyprus account; a genuine German energy-refund or consumer agency would not route payments through a foreign bank account, and this IBAN only passes a formal checksum check — it proves nothing about who actually controls it.

The sender's address is in Nicosia, Cyprus, despite the German-sounding name 'Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie' (Consumer Refund Office for Energy); there is no such official German consumer-refund authority for energy costs.

The letter uses high-pressure wording and a short, hard deadline ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig' — if the deadline passes, your claim is forfeited forever) to rush the recipient into paying without checking — a typical scam tactic.

Do not transfer any money to the IBAN given in this letter. Recommend reporting it to the Verbraucherzentrale and/or the police (Internetwache) and not responding to the sender's phone number or email address printed on the letter.
